title: Angular Momentum

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — System of Particles and Rotational Motion

domain: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
expression: L = Iω   (or L = r × p for a single particle)
explanation: Angular momentum is the rotational analogue of linear momentum: L = Iω for a rigid body rotating with angular velocity ω and moment of inertia I about the axis, or L = r × p for a single particle. When net external torque is zero, L is conserved — this single principle explains a spinning skater speeding up when pulling arms inward (I decreases, ω increases to keep L constant) and underlies Kepler's second law for orbiting planets.

variables.meaning: Moment of inertia about the axis

workedExample.scenario: A skater with I = 4 kg·m² spinning at ω = 2 rad/s pulls arms in, reducing I to 1 kg·m².

commonMistakes: Forgetting angular momentum conservation requires zero NET TORQUE, not zero net force — a central force (through the axis) produces no torque and still allows conservation.
Treating moment of inertia as constant like mass — it changes whenever mass redistributes relative to the axis, which is exactly what makes the skater example work.
genZNote: Pull the arms in, watch the spin speed up — angular momentum conservation, no exceptions.
